To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified QTL and candidate genes for several domestication-related traits of cowpea, including pod shattering, organ size, and seed size.

(1) a high density genetic map was constructed and 16 QTL were identified for 9 domestication-related traits; (2) 4 regions with QTL clusters were identified, including a region on Chr. 8 related to increase organ size; (3) candidate genes were identified for the QTL.
1) a high-density genetic map was constructed and used in QTL mapping; and 2) a total of 16 QTL were identified for nine domestication-related phenotypes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis underlying phenotypic changes associated with cowpea domestication.
the genetic basis of phenotypic variation in domesticated cowpea and its wild progenitors.
understanding how domestication has shaped cowpea.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present study has provided the first genetic map of a recombinant inbreds line population derived from an interspecific cross between a cultivated (V. unguiculatavar. unguicula) and a wild (V. unguiulatavar. dekindtii) accession of cowpea.
the present study has identified several genomic regions controlling important traits in cowpeas.
this work is the first to identify and map the QTL for the domestication-related traits of cowpea.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this study identified 16 quantitative trait locus (QTL) controlling domestication-related phenotypes in cowpea and provided new insights into the genetic architecture of domestication traits in this species.
the genetic basis of the domestication of cowpea was studied by mapping 16 QTL for 9 domestication-related traits.
we identified QTL controlling domesticated traits in a cross between wild and domesticated cowpea and identified candidate genes within these QTL.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the domestication process in cowpea was associated with the accumulation of multiple QTL, and that the domestication-related traits are controlled by different genes.
the domestication of cowpea involved changes in the size and shape of vegetative organs, as well as changes in flower color and pod shattering.
the genetic architecture of domestication-related traits is more complex than previously thought.
